pack: Grade 1 Reading: Main Topic and Key Details

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the passage about bats, circles the main topic word (Bats, Night, Bugs; all three words appear in the text), then answers three written detail questions with a small word bank (night, day, bugs). Supported.
answers: When do bats fly? At night (accept: in the night)
What do many bats eat? Bugs (accept: insects)
When do bats sleep? In the day (accept: during the day)
pages_detail.title: What Is This Text About?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the passage about how a butterfly grows, writes the main topic, then circles the three facts that are in the text from five sentences. Guided.
answers: Main topic: a butterfly (how a butterfly grows)
The egg is on a leaf
A butterfly comes out of a chrysalis
pages_detail.title: Find the Key Details

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the passage about the heart, then answers three written WH questions with a word bank (chest, pumps blood, run and play, rest). Guided.
answers: Where is your heart? In your chest
What does your heart do? It pumps blood all around your body
When does your heart beat fast? When you run and play
pages_detail.title: Ask and Answer

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the passage about the Moon, draws a line to match each cause to what happens (fixed-width boxes, fixed dots, both rows aligned), then writes one why. Guided. The science is simple and accurate: the Sun lights the Moon, and as the Moon moves around the Earth we see more or less of the bright part.
answers: The Sun lights up the Moon. goes to The Moon shines.
The Moon moves around the Earth. goes to It looks different each night.
The Moon shines because the Sun lights it up (accept: because the Sun lights up the Moon)
pages_detail.title: How Are These Facts Connected?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the passage about trains, writes the main topic, then writes three facts learned from the text on three open lines. Word bank only (tracks, engine, cars, stations, people). No sentence starters. Independent.
answers: Any three facts stated in the text, for example: trains run on tracks; the engine pulls the cars; trains stop at stations; people get on and off at a station
pages_detail.title: Tell It Back
